title: Cook's third voyage in the Resolution, 1776–80
summary: Cook took Mai home and then went north to look for a passage round the top of America. He found Hawaiʻi and the Northwest Coast, was turned back by ice off Alaska, and was killed at Kealakekua Bay; Clerke, then Gore, took the ships to Kamchatka, the Bering Strait again and home.

events.label: Queen Charlotte Sound: two Māori boys go with Mai
events.text: Mai took two young New Zealanders from Queen Charlotte Sound as servants: Te Weherua, about seventeen, and Koa, about twelve, who volunteered. They are generally counted the first Māori to travel beyond New Zealand since the great voyages of their ancestors.

events.label: Huahine: Mai is settled
events.text: Cook negotiated with the chiefs of Huahine for land for Mai, and the carpenters built him a house in the European style. He was given furniture, guns and gunpowder, a vineyard, and the two Māori boys as servants.

events.label: Waimea, Kauaʻi: Cook arrives, told twice
events.source: Wikipedia, Cook Landing Site (Waimea); Ka Wai Ola
events.text: From the ships: land was sighted on 18 January and the ships anchored at Waimea on the 19th. Cook landed at the mouth of the Waimea River on the 20th, the first recorded European contact with the Hawaiian Islands. From the shore: Hawaiians paddled out in canoes in the afternoon of the 19th and at first would not come aboard, but talked with the sailors and traded; iron and brass medals were let down to them on a rope. The essays of Lahainaluna students of the 1830s name Kaneoneo and Keawe as the ruling chiefs of Kauaʻi then. It was the season of the Makahiki, the festival of Lono.
events.doubt: Accounts differ on whether first contact came on the 18th or the 19th, and on where Cook came ashore.

events.label: Yuquot, Nootka Sound: a month with the Mowachaht
events.text: From the ships: they anchored in Resolution Cove, off Bligh Island, kept their distance from the village, and watched Mowachaht canoes come out calling 'Itchme nutka!'. They repaired the ships, cut new masts and spars, and traded for some three hundred sea otter pelts. From the village: the Mowachaht, managing their alliances with their neighbours, brought the furs to Yuquot and took home a flood of European goods; the pelts fetched high prices at Kamchatka and Macau, and Yuquot became the first centre of the maritime fur trade. Within a few decades the sea otters were hunted out.
events.doubt: Cook did not record the name of the chief of Yuquot, who may not have been Maquinna, as writers have often assumed.

events.label: Icy Cape: blocked by ice
events.source: Wikipedia, Third voyage of James Cook
events.text: At about 70°N the ice stopped the Resolution and Discovery; there was no passage to be found that year.

events.label: Petropavlovsk: Clerke buried
events.text: Clerke, who died at sea on the passage from the Bering Strait, was buried at Petropavlovsk, in Kamchatka. The Admiralty later set up an obelisk to him there, in 1913.
events.doubt: Sources give the burial as 29 or 30 August 1779.
